Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.1; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Requirement Statement: Factory-default passwords used for user, administrator, recovery, or service access shall be unique per device or replaced through a mandatory initialization process before normal use. Recovery actions shall not reinstate a universal credential.
Verification Objective: Confirm that no shared default credential enables access across devices of the same model.
Required Evidence: Credential lifecycle documentation and secret-safe configuration or behavior observations.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Default credential and recovery-path applicability

Requirement Statement: The device shall allow passwords or passphrases of at least 64 characters without silent truncation, permit password-manager entry, reject commonly used or compromised passwords, and rate-limit failed authentication attempts. It shall not require composition rules based solely on character classes.
Verification Objective: Confirm that password policy resists common online guessing while supporting strong passphrases.
Required Evidence: Password-policy observations and bounded authentication-behavior evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Password policy and online guessing resistance

Normative Source and Locator: NIST SP 800-63B-4 3.1.1.2; OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
Applicability: Where locally stored passwords are used
Requirement Statement: Stored passwords shall use a salted password-hashing scheme with an adaptive work factor, recorded algorithm and parameter metadata, and a migration path for stronger schemes. Secrets shall not be reversibly stored or embedded in firmware configuration.
Verification Objective: Determine whether retained credential material is protected against offline guessing and reversible disclosure.
Required Evidence: Secret-safe account metadata and configuration evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Credential storage and local-account applicability

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces; OWASP ASVS 5.0 authorization requirements
Requirement Statement: The device shall enforce authorization on every management function and state-changing request. An authenticated identity shall receive only the functions and data required for its role and network context.
Verification Objective: Confirm that authentication alone does not grant unauthorized management actions.
Required Evidence: Role, endpoint, and configuration authorization observations.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Authorization bypass and cross-interface privilege boundaries

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6; NISTIR 8259A Device Security
Applicability: Where physical service or debug interfaces are present
Requirement Statement: Unused physical and debug interfaces shall be disabled. A necessary service interface shall require authenticated and authorized access and shall not provide unrestricted system control in the production state.
Verification Objective: Determine whether accessible UART, JTAG, SWD, USB, or similar interfaces bypass normal administrative controls.
Required Evidence: Physical inspection, boot and serial observations, and service-access evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Debug-interface and local-privilege applicability

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Data Protection and Logical Access to Interfaces; ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.5
Requirement Statement: Remote management communications shall provide authentication, integrity, and confidentiality appropriate to the interface. Administrative credentials and session material shall not be exposed over cleartext network protocols.
Verification Objective: Identify cleartext management or credential-bearing exchanges and the protections applied to them.
Required Evidence: Bounded protocol captures and service configuration observations.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Cleartext management and transport protection

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Data Protection and Device Security; NIST SP 800-131A
Applicability: Where cryptography protects data or device trust
Requirement Statement: The device shall use current, publicly reviewed cryptographic algorithms and secure random generation appropriate to the data and protocol. It shall protect private keys and critical security parameters from unauthorized disclosure, modification, and network exposure.
Verification Objective: Assess the design of cryptographic protection without treating an algorithm name alone as proof of security.
Required Evidence: Firmware and configuration observations with exact locators where available.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Cryptographic implementation and key-management applicability

Normative Source and Locator: OWASP ASVS 5.0 session-management requirements; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Applicability: Where web or comparable authenticated sessions are used
Requirement Statement: Sessions shall use unpredictable identifiers, shall not place identifiers in URLs, and shall expire after logout, credential change, and a defined inactivity interval. Cookie-based sessions shall use Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite attribute when applicable.
Verification Objective: Confirm session creation, invalidation, and client-side protections across normal and exceptional flows.
Required Evidence: Router-rendered login, logout, idle-session, and concurrent-session observations.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Session fixation, persistence, and invalidation behavior

Normative Source and Locator: OWASP ASVS 5.0 input-validation and injection-prevention requirements; OWASP ISVS
Applicability: Where a web or API management interface is present
Requirement Statement: Server-side management handlers shall validate untrusted input for its intended syntax and range, handle canonicalization safely, and use safe APIs when data crosses into commands, paths, templates, queries, or parsers. Untrusted input shall not control an interpreter or operating-system command.
Verification Objective: Identify input-to-interpreter and input-to-configuration paths that warrant hypothesis-directed validation.
Required Evidence: Endpoint inventory, request and response schemas, firmware locators, and authorized dynamic evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Command injection, path traversal, parser abuse, and unsafe deserialization

Normative Source and Locator: OWASP ASVS 5.0 output-encoding requirements; OWASP ISVS
Applicability: Where a web or API management interface is present
Requirement Statement: The management interface shall encode or safely sanitize untrusted data for its output context. Untrusted values shall not be inserted into executable, HTML, attribute, URL, or script contexts without context-appropriate protection.
Verification Objective: Identify user-controlled or network-derived values rendered by the management plane.
Required Evidence: Template and response observations with relevant input sources.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Cross-site scripting and client-side injection

Normative Source and Locator: OWASP ASVS 5.0 request-forgery and browser-security requirements
Requirement Statement: State-changing browser requests shall require an anti-forgery control tied to the authenticated session. Cross-origin policy and browser security headers shall not permit untrusted origins to perform or read privileged management actions.
Verification Objective: Assess protection of administrative actions initiated from a browser context.
Required Evidence: Request-flow observations and documented browser-context tests.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Cross-site request forgery and cross-origin management exposure

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Requirement Statement: The product shall maintain an inventory of network listeners and logical interfaces. Services not required for the documented product function shall be disabled, and required services shall minimize unauthenticated disclosure of security-relevant information.
Verification Objective: Establish the reachable service set and compare it with documented or necessary product behavior.
Required Evidence: LAN and WAN service inventories, protocol observations, and firmware service configuration locators.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Unexpected listeners, banner disclosure, and service-to-function traceability

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Requirement Statement: Management services shall not be reachable from untrusted networks by default. Any enabled remote-management path shall require authenticated, authorized access and have an explicit configuration state and network scope.
Verification Objective: Confirm default WAN exposure and whether enabled remote management remains bounded to authorized use.
Required Evidence: LAN and WAN scan results, configuration observations, and service policy evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: WAN administration and network-scope enforcement

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Applicability: Where UPnP, SSDP, IGD, or comparable automatic configuration is supported
Requirement Statement: Automatic network-configuration services shall be disabled by default unless their enabled state is a documented product requirement. When enabled, they shall be restricted to the intended trusted network, operate with least privilege, minimize advertised security-relevant metadata, and shall not expose management services or create unrestricted external reachability.
Verification Objective: Assess discovery, control, and port-mapping behavior without assuming that service presence is a vulnerability.
Required Evidence: Bounded UDP and protocol captures, configuration state, and port-mapping behavior evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: UPnP discovery, authorization, and port-mapping behavior

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Device Configuration; ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.5
Requirement Statement: Only authorized entities shall change security-relevant configuration. Security settings shall have documented secure defaults, configuration import and export shall protect secrets, and security-relevant changes shall be observable to an authorized administrator.
Verification Objective: Evaluate the security of configuration state, transitions, and backup and restore handling.
Required Evidence: Configuration captures, UI behavior, protocol observations, and change records.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Configuration authorization, insecure defaults, and backup and restore handling

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Applicability: Where Wi-Fi access-point functionality is present
Requirement Statement: Wireless security shall use supported modern protocols and cipher suites. The device shall not enable WEP, WPA, or WPA2-TKIP. Wi-Fi Protected Setup shall be disabled by default or absent, and any enabled exception shall have an explicit documented user action.
Verification Objective: Assess wireless defaults and legacy-protocol exposure while preserving product-function context.
Required Evidence: Wireless configuration observations and passive radio evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Legacy wireless security and WPS applicability

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6; NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces
Applicability: Where guest or multiple network zones are supported
Requirement Statement: Guest-network clients shall be prevented by default from reaching the trusted LAN and the device management plane except for explicitly documented services. Client isolation shall be configurable according to the product's documented network model and shall not be presumed for the primary private LAN.
Verification Objective: Evaluate whether advertised guest isolation is enforced in both directions and at the management boundary.
Required Evidence: Guest-network configuration, routing and firewall observations, and authorized isolation-test evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Guest isolation and cross-zone reachability

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Logical Access to Interfaces; ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6
Applicability: Where SSH or another administrative shell service is present
Requirement Statement: Administrative shell services shall be disabled by default. When enabled, they shall restrict access to authorized administrators and approved network scopes, prohibit remote root login, apply rate limiting and inactivity timeout, use secure authentication, and record security-relevant access events.
Verification Objective: Assess whether a shell service expands administrative exposure beyond the documented need.
Required Evidence: Service inventory, configuration, version, and bounded authentication behavior evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Legacy SSH and administrative-shell exposure

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Software Update; ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 secure-update provisions
Requirement Statement: Only authorized entities shall initiate updates. The device shall authenticate and verify each update before installation, reject invalid updates, preserve a failure-safe recovery path, and implement a documented version or rollback policy that prevents unauthorized downgrade to a vulnerable release.
Verification Objective: Assess update authenticity, authorization, integrity verification, and recovery controls as distinct properties.
Required Evidence: Firmware image, update-process observations, signature and version-verification locators, and non-invasive validation evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Firmware authenticity, unauthorized update, and downgrade resistance

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Device Security; ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6
Requirement Statement: The boot chain and executable components shall verify integrity and authenticity before execution using a trust anchor protected from unauthorized modification. The requirement applies to the bootloader, kernel, root filesystem, and other security-relevant components where the architecture supports verification.
Verification Objective: Identify whether component protection exists and define evidence needed before making any claim about its effectiveness.
Required Evidence: Firmware structure, boot observations, and exact integrity-verification locators.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Secure boot and component-integrity applicability

Normative Source and Locator: NISTIR 8259A Cybersecurity State Awareness; ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.6
Requirement Statement: Authorized administrators shall be able to determine the device's security-relevant state, including enabled management services, update state, and configuration changes. Logs and status interfaces shall not expose credentials, session material, or other critical security parameters.
Verification Objective: Assess observability of security state and confidentiality of diagnostic output.
Required Evidence: System log, status interface, and configuration observations.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Security-state awareness and information disclosure

Normative Source and Locator: ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 5.2; NISTIR 8259 R1
Requirement Statement: The manufacturer shall publish a vulnerability-reporting contact and process, define a support period or end-of-support status, and maintain sufficient component and version information to investigate and remediate security defects.
Verification Objective: Provide lifecycle context for remediation and component-risk reasoning without inferring a device vulnerability from component presence alone.
Required Evidence: Vendor policy, version, support, and component-identity evidence.
Related Hypothesis or Test Family: Vulnerability disclosure, support lifecycle, and component-risk triage
